title: vim saves in place: the document keeps its identity and passes through length zero

provenance.evidence: Eight readings. The swap file `.doc.txt.swp` appears (inode 190994899), vanishes, reappears under a NEW inode (190994901) and grows 0 -> 4096 -> 8192 -> 12288. Then `doc.txt` is seen at inode 190994875 with size 26, then the SAME inode at size 0, then the SAME inode at size 6, then the swap vanishes. The document's inode never changes.
provenance.surprise: `backupcopy=no` asks vim to rename the original aside and write a new file, which would change the object's identity. On this APFS volume it did not: the inode is the same before and after, so vim wrote in place anyway. The captured behaviour is what is recorded; the setting's documented behaviour is not.
blind_spots: open, flush, fsync and close are invisible to polling
anything created and removed inside one reading is missed — the first swap file was caught only because it survived a reading

objects.role: doc.txt, the document — one identity throughout

folder.fidelity: a backend that does not declare ObserveDurableBoundary
folder.omission_note: The swap file's whole life may fall between two readings.

expected.meaningful_durable_change: doc.txt holds the edited text and no swap file exists. The document's identity is unchanged, so nothing about this save is a replacement.
expected.forbidden_note: Mount sequence 5 and folder sequence 4 are the SAME captured state: the document exists, is the same object, and is EMPTY. It was measured, not imagined — reading 6 of the capture shows doc.txt at inode 190994875 with size 0. A checkpoint there is a durable record of the person having deleted the contents of their file.

notes: On a mount, the Closed at sequence 7 anchors the checkpoint and the empty state is never a candidate: the rule is safe here because the backend can prove where the save ended.

On a folder-watching backend there is NO candidate anywhere in this stream, so the only thing that ends the window is quiescence. If the process is killed between folder sequences 4 and 5, the last durable state is the empty document, and Mesh has no way to know it was mid-save. That is exactly the restriction already shipped as FALLBACK_NO_SAVE_POINT_FROM_THE_FOLDER, met from the other direction.

The truncate at sequence 5 is not expressible at mesh-workspace-adapter/0: there is no truncate and no size in PortableMetadata (01KZHAGG8Q83Q0YBHGDXSS8J1M). It is recorded here as the two Written events a backend would emit, because that is what the corpus can honestly say.
